title: Targeting TNFR1 by salvianolic acid B alleviates sepsis-induced acute lung injury and pulmonary-intestinal epithelial barrier damage.
authors: Ma, Luyao; Liu, Fanglin; Shen, Jingjing; Wu, Jianchao; Sun, Jinxia; Lu, Zhenhui; Jiang, Xin
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究丹酚酸B靶向TNFR1缓解脓毒症肺肠损伤，虽含分子对接但核心为湿实验药效机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (ALI) and intestinal injury were characterized by dysregulated systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction. Host-directed therapy (HDT) that modulates excessive immune responses is a promising complementary strategy. Salvianolic acid B (Sal B) has been reported to modulate various signaling pathways, yet whether it targets TNFR1 to simultaneously inhibit NF-kappaB, necroptosis, and p-MLCK/p-MLC2 in septic ALI remains unexplored. PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of Sal B against sepsis-induced lung-intestine injury and to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms, with a focus on identifying its potential cellular target. METHODS: A murine model of sepsis-induced ALI was established via lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge. H&E staining, ELISA, immunohistochemistry analyses were performed to assess lung, intestinal injury and their barrier damage. In vitro, models of LPS/zVAD-induced macrophage necroptosis and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) induced epithelial barrier damage were established in J774A.1, THP-1, A549, and HCT116 cells. Cell death, cytokine secretion, the key proteins of necroptosis and signal molecules related to epithelial barrier integrity were evaluated using LDH/PI assays, ELISA, western blotting, and immunofluorescence. By using gene silencing and overexpression techniques, the role of tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (TNFR1) in regulating the necrotic apoptosis process of macrophages infected with LPS was elucidated. The Sal B-TNFR1 potential interaction was validated using drug target identification methods such as molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis. RESULTS: In vivo, Sal B alleviated pulmonary edema, histopathological damage in lung and colon, and reduced systemic and local levels of TNF-alpha and interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta). It concurrently suppressed the activation of the phospho myosin light-chain kinase/phospho myosin light chain 2 (p-MLCK/p-MLC2) pathway and restored expression of tight junction proteins, while inhibiting the necroptosis pathway. In vitro, Sal B inhibited TNF-alpha-induced barrier damage in epithelial cells and LPS/zVAD-induced necroptosis in macrophages. Mechanistically, Sal B exhibits a strong binding potential with TNFR1 and may exert protective effects by targeting TNFR1 to modulate necroptosis and pulmonary and intestinal epithelial barrier damage, ultimately attenuating LPS-induced the lung-intestine injury. CONCLUSION: By potentially targeting TNFR1, Sal B exerts protective effects on both lung and intestine. These findings underscore the therapeutic potential of Sal B as a novel HDT strategy.
abstract_zh: 背景：脓毒症诱导的急性肺损伤（ALI）和肠道损伤以系统性炎症失调和器官功能障碍为特征。调节过度免疫反应的宿主导向治疗（HDT）是一种有前景的补充策略。丹酚酸B（Sal B）已被报道可调节多种信号通路，但其是否靶向TNFR1以同时抑制脓毒症ALI中的NF-kappaB、坏死性凋亡及p-MLCK/p-MLC2，仍待探索。目的：本研究旨在探讨Sal B对脓毒症诱导的肺-肠损伤的保护作用，并阐明其潜在分子机制，重点在于识别其可能的细胞靶点。方法：通过脂多糖（LPS）攻击建立脓毒症诱导的ALI小鼠模型。采用H&E染色、ELISA、免疫组织化学分析评估肺、肠道损伤及其屏障破坏。体外实验中，在J774A.1、THP-1、A549和HCT116细胞中建立LPS/zVAD诱导的巨噬细胞坏死性凋亡模型及肿瘤坏死因子-alpha（TNF-alpha）诱导的上皮屏障损伤模型。通过LDH/PI检测、ELISA、western blotting和免疫荧光评估细胞死亡、细胞因子分泌、坏死性凋亡关键蛋白及与上皮屏障完整性相关的信号分子。利用基因沉默和过表达技术，阐明肿瘤坏死因子受体1（TNFR1）在调节LPS感染巨噬细胞坏死性凋亡过程中的作用。通过分子对接和定点突变等药物靶点鉴定方法验证Sal B-TNFR1的潜在相互作用。结果：在体内，Sal B减轻了肺水肿、肺和结肠的组织病理学损伤，并降低了TNF-alpha和白细胞介素-1beta（IL-1beta）的系统及局部水平。同时，它抑制了磷酸化肌球蛋白轻链激酶/磷酸化肌球蛋白轻链2（p-MLCK/p-MLC2）通路的激活，恢复了紧密连接蛋白的表达，并抑制了坏死性凋亡通路。在体外，Sal B抑制了TNF-alpha诱导的上皮细胞屏障损伤及LPS/zVAD诱导的巨噬细胞坏死性凋亡。机制上，Sal B与TNFR1表现出强结合潜力，可能通过靶向TNFR1调节坏死性凋亡及肺和肠上皮屏障损伤，最终减轻LPS诱导的肺-肠损伤。结论：通过潜在靶向TNFR1，Sal B对肺和肠道均发挥保护作用。这些发现强调了Sal B作为一种新型HDT策略的治疗潜力。
